title: The Fisherman and the Little Fish
summary: An elderly fisherman sat upon a stone pier casting his line into the sea all morning without success.. Facing a decisive turning point, the characters discover that a small certainty in hand is worth far more than a grand promise in the future.
keywords: the fisherman and the little fish
full_text:
Across the rocky pastures and olive orchards of ancient Greece, a memorable encounter unfolded. An elderly fisherman sat upon a stone pier casting his line into the sea all morning without success. The surrounding valley lay quiet in the midday heat, yet within the peaceful scene, natural instincts and rival interests were quietly at work.

Before long, the initial quiet gave way to a sharp challenge as unexpected circumstances forced both sides to act. At noon, his cork bobbed under, and he pulled up a tiny sprat no bigger than his thumb. As the fisherman prepared to toss the tiny catch into his willow basket, the little fish opened his mouth and gasped: "Have pity, fisherman! Each party sought to press their advantage, weighing spoken words against unspoken motives.

When the decisive moment arrived, neither boastful pretense nor hasty excuses could alter the outcome. Look at how small I am—I am barely a single bite for a hungry man! Throw me back into the cool ocean waves! Let me swim and grow fat for another season; then you may catch me again and sell me at the harbor market for a silver coin!" The old fisherman slipped the little fish into his creel, secured the wicker lid, and replied with a serene smile: "I should be a fool indeed to surrender a small fish already in my basket on the doubtful chance of catching a larger one in the stormy future!" The experience left behind a timeless truth for all who heard the tale, demonstrating that a small certainty in hand is worth far more than a grand promise in the future.
moral: A small certainty in hand is worth far more than a grand promise in the future.
